attribs.name: repeating_traits_-O7oM7gQCd7aqWwCZDQt_description
attribs.current:
As a master of illusion and mental manipulation, you can cast mesmer spells. Your magic weaves complex illusions and manipulates the minds of those around you, bending perceptions to your will and controlling the flow of battle through cunning and subtlety.

Cantrips p3[–] At 1st level, you know three cantrips of your choice from the mesmer spell list. You gain additional mesmer cantrips of your choice at higher levels, as shown in the Cantrips Known column of the Mesmer table.

Preparing and Casting Spells p3[–] The Mesmer table shows how many spell slots you have to cast your mesmer spells of 1st level and higher. To cast one of these spells, you must expend a slot of the spell's level or higher. You regain all expended spell slots when you finish a long rest.

You prepare the list of mesmer spells that are available for you to cast, choosing from the mesmer spell list. When you do so, choose a number of mesmer spells equal to your Intelligence modifier + your mesmer level (minimum of one spell). The spells must be of a level for which you have spell slots.

For example, if you are a 3rd-level mesmer, you have four 1st-level and two 2nd-level spell slots. With an Intelligence of 16, your list of prepared spells can include six spells of 1st or 2nd level, in any combination. If you prepare the 1st-level spell illusionary force, you can cast it using a 1st-level or 2nd-level slot. Casting the spell doesn't remove it from your list of prepared spells.

You can change your list of prepared spells when you finish a long rest. Preparing a new list of mesmer spells requires time spent in meditation and mental exercises: at least 1 minute per spell level for each spell on your list.

Spellcasting Ability p3[–] Intelligence is your spellcasting ability for your mesmer spells, as your magic hinges on your ability to deceive, manipulate, and outsmart. You use your Intelligence whenever a spell refers to your spellcasting ability. In addition, you use your Intelligence modifier when setting the saving throw DC for a mesmer spell you cast and when making an attack roll with one.

Spell save DC = 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Intelligence modifier

Spell attack modifier = your proficiency bonus + your Intelligence modifier

Ritual Casting p3[–] You can cast any mesmer spell you know as a ritual if that spell has the ritual tag and you have the spell prepared.

Spellcasting Focus p3[–] You can use an arcane focus as a spellcasting focus for your mesmer spells. Mesmers often use objects that reflect their personal flair and the theatrical nature of their magic, such as mirrors, masks, or crystal orbs, as their arcane focuses. To use such an item, you must spend an hour in concentration, imbuing it with your magical essence.

attribs.name: repeating_traits_-O7oM7gVpwGGOKd2-SUD_description
attribs.current: Harnessing your mastery over illusion, you have the unique ability to create and manipulate clones of yourself to confuse, distract, and damage your enemies. These replicas are fundamental to your tactics, providing both offensive and defensive capabilities.

attribs.name: repeating_traits_-O7oM7gZU1uC9UYc1x0y_description
attribs.current:
At 2nd level, your mastery over illusions deepens, granting you the power to shatter your clones for devastating effects. Each shatter ability triggers a unique effect that scales with the number of clones you shatter.

Shatter Style[–] Using a bonus action, you can shatter any number of your active clones within 60 feet. The effects of shattering are enhanced by the number of clones shattered, as defined in each shatter style below.

**Mind Wrack**. Deal psychic damage to all creatures of your choice within 5ft of each shattered clone. Damage each clone deals increases with the number of clones shattered: 1d6 for one clone, 2d6 for two clones, {dice 4d6} for three clones, doubling the dice for each additional clone shattered. Creatures must succed on an Intelligence saving throw against your Spell Save DC to take half damage.

A creature adjacent to multiple clones will take a seperate instance of damage from each shattered clone.

**Cry of Frustration**. Shatter your clones to inflict confusion on creatures of your choice near the clones. Each creature that is within 5ft of a shattered clone must make a wisdom saving throw against your Spell Save DC or be confused till the end of its next turn. Creatures next to multiple clones need to make multiple saving throws but will only be affected by one source of confused

A confused creature is muddled with defening thoughts as the clone's cries ring out. It may use its action to focus and end the confusion. If it uses its action, bonus action, movement or reaction to do anything else while confused, it takes 1d8 psychic damage. The damage taken increases with the number of clones shattered. 1d8 for one clone, 2d8 for two clones, 3d8 for three clones and so on. 

**Diversion**. Shatter your clones to daze and disrupts your enemies. Each creature that is adjacent to a clone must make a dexterity saving throw against your spell save DC or immediately lose thier reactions. Creatures next to multiple clones need to make multiple saving throws. If a creature was concentrating, it also needs to make a contitution saving throw to maintain concentration. The DC for which is enhanced by the number of clones you shatter. DC 10 + Shattered clones. 

**Distortion**. Shatter your clones to and grant yourself a moment of invulnerability. You gain a pool of d6's that you can use to reduce damage dealt to you. The pool is as large as the number of clones shattered.

When you take damage, you can roll dice from this pool and reduce the damage by that amount after any reductions from resistance.

attribs.name: repeating_traits_-O7oM7gdDZWwwxIxTYl4_description
attribs.current:
At 6th level, your mastery over illusions allows you to weave them into more complex and damaging forms. Your illusions are now capable of executing a simultaneous double attack, overwhelming your foes with a barrage of strikes from multiple angles.

Enhanced Clone Attack[–] Whenever you use your 'I'm The Real One!!!' ability to command one of your clones to attack, you can now make a second attack with another clone against the same target or a different one within range. Each attack uses your spell attack modifier and deals psychic damage equal to 1d4 + your Intelligence modifier.

Tactical Reposition p8[–] Whenever you create a clone using any of your abilities, you can choose to swap places with any one of your existing clones within 60ft. This swap can be triggered once per turn, allowing you to reposition strategically without provoking opportunity attacks.

attribs.name: repeating_traits_-O7oM90wGOMW9S9NkHEC_description
attribs.current:
Your mastery of deception and control over illusion magic has unveiled the true nature of the archfey, the powerful beings who govern vast regions of the Feywild, including the laws of physics and temporality within their domains. By tapping into the magic of the Feywild, you enhance your clones and gain the ability to create wells that channel this mystical energy.

Feywild Wells[–] 3rd-level Chronomancer feature

Your connection to the Feywild allows you to channel its magical energy into wells of the Feywild. When you create a clone, you can choose to instead to create a well where the clone was about to appear. At 3rd level you gain access to the following two wells with more as you gain levels in this subclass.

Fey Well of Protection: As an action, you can create a 10-foot-radius well at a point you can see within 30 feet. This well lasts for 1 minute. Allies within the well have advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects and gain temporary hit points equal to your Mesmer level at the start of each of their turns. You can use this feature as many times as your proficiency bonus per long rest.

Fey Well of Illusions: As an action, you can create a 10-foot-radius well at a point you can see within 30 feet. This well lasts for 1 minute. Enemies within the well have disadvantage on saving throws against your spells and mesmer effects. Additionally, illusions you create within the well are semi-tangible, allowing them to interact with the environment and creatures. These illusions can support up to 10 pounds of weight and have disadvantage on checks to see through them. You can use this feature once per short or long rest.

Phantasm[–] 3rd-level Chronomancer feature

Instead of creating clones out of illusion magic, you pull past phantasms of yourself out of time. These phantasms behave like your clones but have hitpoints equal to a fifth of your max and cannot be discerned by tremorsense.

attribs.name: repeating_traits_-O7oM91-3wgwivVmm7Mk_description
attribs.current:
6th-level Chronomancer feature

Once per long rest, as an action, you can activate a flux state in an area around you, causing a barrage of rapid gravity disturbances. For the next minute, you control gravity in an area 30ft around you and can produce the following effects as an Action/Bonus action or both:
--------------------
- Choose two creatures/objects weighing less than 400lbs within the flux and force them to make a strength saving throw. Each creature on a failure is pulled 15ft towards the other.
---------------------
- Choose one creature within the flux and force it to make a constitution saving throw. On a failure, its weight increases by 500%. A creature's speed is set to 0 if its weight becomes higher than 1000lbs. Otherwise, its speed is halved till the end of its next turn.
-----------------
- Increase your local gravity to induce gravitational wells. Each creature within the area must make a dexterity saving throw or be moved in a 90 degree arc (you choose between clockwise and anti-clockwise) with respect to you. To resolve circular movement, draw a 90 degree cone with you as the center and the affected creature as one of the sides of the cone. Move the creature to the corresponding space on the other side of the cone.
----------------
- Choose up to three creatures within the flux. Each target must make a strength saving throw or be pushed 20 feet away from you.
-----------------
- Choose up to three creatures. Each target gains 60ft flying speed in the flux as you manipulate gravity around them till the end of your next turn.
-------------------
- Choose an object weighing up to 1000 lbs times your level. You can move it up to 30 feet in any direction.

attribs.name: repeating_traits_-O7oMKeeszKYhKOJXejX_description
attribs.current:
At 1st level, you gain the Replicate ability, allowing you to create clones. A clone mimics your actions (including movement) and serves as a distraction, it has the same AC as you had at the moment it was created, having 1 hit point and causing direct attacks against it to be made with disadvantage. It uses your modifiers and ability scores to make saving throws.

Creatures that do not have truesight, blindsight or tremorsense and can see these clones are unable to discern them from you. When they pick you as a target for an effect or an attack and there are one or more clones within range, the target is picked at random. If more than one target can be selected, multiple clones can be subject to the effect. A creature that uses an action to make a successful perception check against your Spell Save DC will be able to discern the clones that exist from you.

At any point, you can have as many clones active as your proficiency bonus.

attribs.current:
You cast sorcerous energy at one creature or object within range. Make a ranged attack roll against the target. On a hit, the target takes d8 damage. If you roll an 8 on the d8 for this spell, you can roll another d8, and add it to the damage.

Whenever you cast this spell, the maximum number of these d8s you can add to the spell's damage equals your spellcasting ability modifier. You choose the damage type each time you cast this spell: Acid, Cold, Fire, Lightning, Poison, Psychic or Thunder.

This spell's damage increases by 1d8 when you reach 5th level (2d8), 11th level (3d8), and 17th level (4d8).

- One Medium or smaller creature that you choose must succeed on a Strength saving throw or be pushed up to 5 feet away from you.

A Large quasi-real, horselike creature appears on the ground in an unoccupied space of your choice within range. You decide the creature's appearance, but it is equipped with a saddle, bit, and bridle. Any of the equipment created by the spell vanishes in a puff of smoke if it is carried more than 10 feet away from the steed.

For the duration, you or a creature you choose can ride the steed. The creature uses the statistics for a riding horse, except it has a speed of 100 feet and can travel 10 miles in an hour, or 13 miles at a fast pace. When the spell ends, the steed gradually fades, giving the rider 1 minute to dismount. The spell ends if you use an action to dismiss it or if the steed takes any damage.

attribs.current:
You unleash a shimmering lance of psychic power from your forehead at a creature that you can see within range. Alternatively, you can utter a creature's name. If the named target is within range, it becomes the spell's target even if you can't see it. If the named target isn't within range, the lance dissipates without effect.

The target must make an Intelligence saving throw. On a failed save, the target takes 7d6 psychic damage and is incapacitated until the start of your next turn. On a successful save, the creature takes half as much damage and isn't incapacitated.

attribs.name: repeating_spell-1_-O7oXxkalAUwt1V8ebdA_spelldescription
attribs.current:
You create the image of an object, a creature, or some other visible phenomenon that is no larger than a 15-foot cube. The image appears at a spot within range and lasts for the duration. The image is purely visual; it isn't accompanied by sound, smell, or other sensory effects.

You can use your action to cause the image to move to any spot within range. As the image changes location, you can alter its appearance so that its movements appear natural for the image. For example, if you create an image of a creature and move it, you can alter the image so that it appears to be walking.

Physical interaction with the image reveals it to be an illusion, because things can pass through it. A creature that uses its action to examine the image can determine that it is an illusion with a successful Intelligence (Investigation) check against your spell save DC. If a creature discerns the illusion for what it is, the creature can see through the image.

When you target a creature who is rolling death saves with this spell, it gains 1 hitpoint. The target may then roll upto half their max hitdie and along with the result, add the spellcasting modifier for each hitdie rolled and gain that many temporary hitpoints.

Until the start of the target's second turn, it has advantage on all saving throws, resistance to all instances of damage, advantage on all attack rolls and has the effects of any existing conditions suppressed except for petrified, invisible and prone.

At the start of the second turn the target will lose all temporary hitpoints gained from this spell and gain 4 levels of exhaustion. Additionally, until its next long rest, it will die after only failing one death save.

attribs.name: repeating_spell-cantrip_-O7ovZH1N1zSRaJTPA-J_spelldescription
attribs.current:
You create a sound or an image of an object within range that lasts for the duration. The illusion also ends if you dismiss it as an action or cast this spell again.

If you create a sound, its volume can range from a whisper to a scream. It can be your voice, someone else's voice, a lion's roar, a beating of drums, or any other sound you choose. The sound continues unabated throughout the duration, or you can make discrete sounds at different times before the spell ends.

If you create an image of an object—such as a chair, muddy footprints, or a small chest—it must be no larger than a 5-foot cube. The image can't create sound, light, smell, or any other sensory effect. Physical interaction with the image reveals it to be an illusion, because things can pass through it.

If a creature uses its action to examine the sound or image, the creature can determine that it is an illusion with a successful Intelligence (Investigation) check against your spell save DC. If a creature discerns the illusion for what it is, the illusion becomes faint to the creature.

You choose a point within range and cause psychic energy to explode there. Each creature in a 20-foot-radius sphere centered on that point must make an Intelligence saving throw. A creature with an Intelligence score of 2 or lower can't be affected by this spell. A target takes 8d6 psychic damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.

After a failed save, a target has muddled thoughts for 1 minute. During that time, it rolls a d6 and subtracts the number rolled from all its attack rolls and ability checks, as well as its Constitution saving throws to maintain concentration. The target can make an Intelligence saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.
